steps.title: Extract insect genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate total DNA from each brown planthopper (≈3 mg dry weight) using the GF‑1 Tissue DNA Extraction Kit (Vivantis). Process no more than 20 insects at a time.

substeps.instruction: Place frozen insects (−20 °C, stored in absolute ethanol) on a Petri plate, remove wings with a sterile blade, and transfer each to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Grind each insect in liquid nitrogen and homogenize in 250 µL Tissue Lysis (TL) buffer with a sterile micro‑pestle.
Briefly vortex, add 3 µL RNase A (10 mg/mL), seal with Parafilm, and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min in a water bath.
Add 20 µL proteinase K (20 mg/mL) and 12 µL lysis enhancer, invert gently, and incubate at 65 °C for 2–3 h until fully dissolved.
Add ~600 µL Tissue Binding (TB) buffer (two volumes), mix, and incubate at 65 °C for 10 min.
Add 200 µL absolute ethanol, vortex quickly to homogenize.
Transfer ~600 µL of the mixture to the spin column in a clean collection tube and centrifuge at 7 000 g for 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Repeat the transfer and centrifugation for the remaining lysate.
Wash column with 600 µL wash buffer, centrifuge at 7 000 g for 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Perform a short dry spin to remove residual ethanol; discard flow‑through.
Place column in a fresh 1.5 mL tube, add 36 µL pre‑warmed elution buffer (EB) to the column centre, let stand 5 min at room temperature (28–37 °C), then spin at 19 000 g for 1 min.
Collect eluate containing purified DNA.

steps.title: Assess insect DNA quality
steps.instruction: Check DNA integrity, purity and concentration by agarose gel electrophoresis and NanoDrop spectrophotometry.

substeps.instruction: Run 0.8 % TBE agarose gel and visualize DNA bands.
Measure absorbance on a NanoDrop; accept samples with 260/280 ≥ 1.8 and 260/230 ≥ 1.8.
Typical yield per adult BPH is 1.5–2 µg. Keep DNA on ice and store at −20 °C until further use.

steps.title: Extract plant genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate total DNA from rice tissue using the GeneJET Plant Genomic DNA Purification Mini Kit (Thermo Scientific) or any equivalent plant DNA kit.

substeps.instruction: Grind 100 mg plant tissue in liquid nitrogen to a fine powder.
Transfer powder to a 1.5 mL tube containing 350 µL lysis buffer A; vortex 15 s and mix thoroughly.
Add 50 µL lysis buffer B and RNase A (provided), then incubate 10 min at 65 °C with occasional vortexing.
Add 130 µL precipitation solution, invert 1–3 times, and incubate on ice for 5 min.
Centrifuge at 22 000 g for 5 min; transfer supernatant to a clean tube.
Add 400 µL Plant gDNA Binding solution and 400 µL 96 % ethanol; mix well.
Load half of the mixture onto the spin column, centrifuge at 7 000 g for 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Apply the remaining mixture to the same column and centrifuge 1 min at 7 000 g.
Add 500 µL Wash Buffer I (reconstituted in absolute ethanol), centrifuge 1 min at 11 500 g; discard flow‑through.
Add 500 µL Wash Buffer II, centrifuge 3 min at 22 000 g; discard flow‑through.
Perform a dry spin at full speed for 1 min to remove residual ethanol.
Elute DNA with 100 µL pre‑warmed EB placed at the column centre, incubate 5 min at room temperature (28–37 °C), then centrifuge 1 min at 11 200 g.
Collect eluate; keep on ice and store at −20 °C.

steps.title: Quantify DNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: Determine concentrations of extracted insect and plant DNA using the Qubit 4.0 fluorometer and dsDNA Broad Range kit.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Qubit working solution by diluting reagent 1:200 in buffer.
Add 198 µL working solution to each Qubit assay tube.
Add 2 µL DNA sample to the tube, vortex to mix (final volume 200 µL).
Incubate tubes at room temperature (28–37 °C) for 2 min.
On the Qubit, select dsDNA → Broad Range (or High Sensitivity) assay.
Press “Read Samples”, choose the sample volume added, and set output units to ng/µL.
Insert each tube into the sample chamber, close lid, and press “Read Tube”.
Record the reported concentration for each sample before proceeding to the next.

steps.title: Check DNA quality by agarose gel
steps.instruction: Run 0.8 % TBE agarose gel to verify DNA integrity and estimate concentration ranges (20–60 ng/µL for insects, 50–150 ng/µL for plants).

steps.title: Purify PCR 16S rRNA fragments
steps.instruction: Purify the 618 bp PCR amplicons from insect samples using the GF‑1 AmbiClean Gel & PCR kit (Vivantis) or any equivalent DNA gel extraction kit.

substeps.instruction: Run PCR products on an agarose gel, locate the 618 bp band, and excise it with a sterile blade (minimize UV exposure).
Transfer the gel slice to a pre‑weighed Eppendorf tube and record its net weight.
Add DB buffer at 1 vol per 0.1 g gel (e.g., 100 µL DB buffer for a 0.1 g slice).
Incubate at 50 °C with occasional mixing until the gel dissolves completely.
Add an equal volume of absolute ethanol, vortex quickly for 5 s.
Load the mixture onto the DNA binding column and centrifuge at 13 500 g for 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Add 650 µL wash buffer, centrifuge 13 500 g for 1 min; discard flow‑through.
Perform a short dry spin to remove residual ethanol.
Place the column in a fresh tube, add 36 µL elution buffer (EB) to the column centre, let stand 5 min at room temperature (28–37 °C), then spin at 13 500 g for 1 min.
Collect eluate containing purified PCR DNA.

steps.title: Quantify purified PCR product
steps.instruction: Measure concentration of the purified 618 bp amplicon using the Qubit dsDNA Assay BR kit on the Qubit 4.0 fluorometer.

substeps.instruction: Follow the kit protocol; expected concentration is 10–15 ng/µL with >80 % recovery.

steps.title: Sequence PCR fragments (Nanopore)
steps.instruction: Submit the purified amplicons for sequencing on an Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) platform (alternatively PacBio).

steps.title: Perform statistical analyses
steps.instruction: Analyze sequencing data to identify Pseudomonas species and assess community differences using the specified statistical tests.

substeps.instruction: Evaluate beta‑diversity clustering significance with PERMANOVA (p ≤ 0.001).
Identify differentially abundant species with DESeq2 (adjusted p ≤ 0.05).
Conduct univariate analysis to rank the top 50 species showing significant abundance variation.
Apply Kruskal‑Wallis test (p ≤ 0.05) followed by Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) to calculate effect sizes of differentially abundant species.
All analyses are performed with R scripts integrated in MicrobiomeAnalyst.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for Pseudomonas-specific 16S rRNA gut-microbiome profiling of the brown planthopper populations (BPH) collected from different geographical regions and across seasons. Additionally, this protocol can be successfully extended for screening and understanding the microbiome dynamics in the populations of other insect pests.
